body:
Just because these players were not dealt at the deadline, that does not mean they will suit up for their current team in 2027
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:49 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The deals that got across the finish line at the 2026 NFL trade deadline included a couple of blockbusters that shook up the balance of power at the front of the Super Bowl race. But just as meaningful were the moves that never materialized. For instance, the Cincinnati Bengals and Philadelphia Eagles called off an agreed-upon transaction that would have bolstered the former's defense. Even more significant than the nixed Arnold Ebiketie deal were the offers for Jonathan Taylor and other stars that never resulted in trades, either.Taylor was supposed to be the belle of the ball at the deadline, but the Indianapolis Colts turned down interest from other teams when they did not receive the first-round pick they sought in a return package. Stars like George Pickens and other players like Will McDonald IV who would have been plug-and-play starters on other teams remained in place on their present rosters.The players teams made and entertained calls on but did not switch at the deadline immediately became names to monitor ahead of the next trade window, which opens in the spring at the start of the 2027 league year.Here are the 10 biggest names that did not change teams at the trade deadline but who could be on the move in the offseason.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Jonathan Taylor, RB, ColtsThe Indianapolis Colts were the most aggressive sellers at the trade deadline, but Jonathan Taylor was not among the four players they shipped out of town. The three-time Pro Bowler is a gargantuan asset because he is an elite-tier running back with no guaranteed money on his contract in 2027 or 2028, so he can remain an affordable and prolific foundational piece of the Colts' rebuild. Those same factors make him tremendously valuable on the trade market, though, and for a team that is going nowhere fast, it would behoove the Colts to take the right deal if it came to them in the offseason. They reportedly turned down offers that included second-round picks and more, so it will probably take at least a first-rounder to pry him away next spring or summer.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    George Pickens, WR, CowboysUnless the Dallas Cowboys re-sign George Pickens, they may regret not trading him. They likely could have garnered a sizable return package for their No. 2 wide receiver -- who would be a No. 1 on most teams -- and that would have arguably been the more prudent move than keeping him on a squad that is on the outside looking in on the playoff picture. Jerry Jones declined to sign Pickens to a long-term extension last offseason and could again use the franchise tag on the standout pass-catcher, but Pickens is worthy of a lucrative multi-year deal and may seek one elsewhere if Jones is hesitant again.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Will McDonald IV, EDGE, JetsWill McDonald IV requested a trade from the New York Jets on the eve of the trade deadline, citing frustration with his playing time. He played 50% or more of the team's defensive snaps just three times over the first nine weeks and most recently saw only 24 snaps of work in Week 9. Darren Mougey did not heed his request, though, and retained him despite reported interest from other teams, including the Jacksonville Jaguars. New York has myriad options at edge rusher and will feature David Bailey most prominently in the years to come, so a clear path to a larger role may not manifest for McDonald. In that case, he could amplify his search for a trade in the offseason.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Khalil Mack, EDGE, ChargersA reunion between Khalil Mack and the Chicago Bears would have made all the sense in the world, but the Los Angeles Chargers showed no interest in moving him, and the Bears used their draft capital on Jeffery Simmons instead. That the Chargers held onto all but one player despite their putrid 0-8 record was a major surprise. There were draft picks to be had for Mack, Ladd McConkey and even Justin Herbert, but the Chargers elected to keep their core intact even as it looks unsalvageable in a miserable campaign. Mack is a prime candidate to walk in free agency since he is in the latter stages of his career and would thus be more likely to seek a home on a contending squad rather than a bottom-dweller like Los Angeles.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Tony Pollard, RB, TitansTeams inquired about Tony Pollard, but none constructed a trade package strong enough for the Tennessee Titans to move on from him. The 29-year-old's value has never been higher on the heels of back-to-back 100-yard performances in which he totaled five touchdowns, and that could have played a role in the Titans driving a hard bargain. Retaining him is a short-term play that will allow Tennessee to continue to evaluate second-year quarterback Cam Ward but may not be much more than that since Pollard can leave in free agency if he pleases. At 29, he is not on the same career timeline as the rest of the team's offensive building blocks, anyway.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Brian Thomas Jr., WR, JaguarsIt makes ample sense for the Jacksonville Jaguars to hold onto anyone and everyone as they prepare for a potential Super Bowl run. If it ain't broke, don't fix it. But Brian Thomas Jr. is only a marginal part of their stellar passing attack and lost ground to Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers in the pecking order for targets. His Pro Bowl-caliber rookie season looks more and more like a flash in the pan. Unless the Jaguars truly believe they can maximize the former first-round pick's talent in the final year of his contract, his situation will be one to revisit in the next trade window that opens in March. This is not dissimilar to the situation that led to Marvin Harrison Jr. being traded to the Houston Texans for a second-round pick and sixth-rounder, but the Jaguars are a contender and would reasonably prefer not to toy with their lineup until after the season.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Budda Baker, S, CardinalsBudda Baker is an Arizona Cardinals legend. If the 2026 trade deadline—when the Cardinals are projected as potential sellers amid on-field struggles —was not the time to move him, they may just let him play out his career in the desert. As the Cardinals' roster continues to shift in a younger direction, though, a split could make sense. Baker will be 31 when the 2027 league year begins, and the Cardinals are poised to take a quarterback in the first round of the draft, restarting the clock on their contention timeline. As an eight-time Pro Bowler still in his prime, Baker would garner the kind of return that would help Arizona load up on draft picks and build around that incoming quarterback.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Riq Woolen, CB, EaglesAs with the other trade candidates on expiring deals, Riq Woolen's potential exit in free agency could net the Philadelphia Eagles a valuable compensatory draft pick. That is probably the justification for keeping him, because Howie Roseman was willing to move on from some foundational pieces in the weeks leading up to the deadline, and Woolen seemed as tradeable as any of them. Woolen has been solid for the Eagles in pass defense but regressed from the standout level he performed at with the Seattle Seahawks -- his 103.3 passer rating allowed is by far a career-worst -- so Philadelphia may not aim to retain him on a multi-year deal regardless.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Josh Sweat, EDGE, CardinalsThere have been rumblings of a possible Josh Sweat trade since the spring. Nothing came to fruition in the offseason, and the Arizona Cardinals stood pat at the trade deadline, too. But as the team remains mired in the early stages of a deep rebuild, any tensions between Sweat and the front office may grow louder in advance of his next opportunity to seek a way out. Sweat reportedly requested a trade last spring amid frustration with his contract, but both he and the team worked to quell that narrative over the last handful of months. It is clear that moving him is not a top priority for the Cardinals, but the standout pass rusher will be one to keep monitoring at the start of the new league year in 2027 in case that changes.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Calvin Ridley, WR, TitansThe Tennessee Titans have phased Calvin Ridley out of their receiving corps, with Carnell Tate, Wan'Dale Robinson, Elic Ayomanor, and Chimere Dike outproducing him in catches. Two tight ends and two running backs also have more targets than him this season. If he is no longer part of their plans, it makes little sense to retain him for the final year of his $92 million contract. His dead cap hit shrinks from $22.5 million to $7.5 million this spring, so if the idea behind keeping him on the roster is to maximize future financial flexibility, that decrease in liability should free things up on the books enough to move on from him at the start of the next league year.

This year, fans will get both. The Bloodline and 946 will engage in WarGames; meanwhile, Cody Rhodes captains Team USA against Rey Mysterio's Team Mexico in a traditional Survivor Series match. In December, the second annual Wrestlepalooza hits The Land Down Under. WWE has ambitions of making Wrestlepalooza a big deal. Last year, the card opened with John Cena vs. Brock Lesnar as part of Cena's retirement tour, plus AJ Lee's first match in a decade, teaming with her husband CM Punk against Seth Rollins and Becky Lynch. Speaking of Cena, the record-breaking WWE world champion returns two days after Wrestlepalooza. title: UFC 334: Ciryl Gane brushes off dirty fighter label, but others are convinced - CBS Sports

NEW YORK -- When Ciryl Gane enters a room, it's difficult to miss the youthful joy that radiates off the smile of the muscular, 6-foot-5 UFC heavyweight champion. After all, the 36-year-old Gane (14-2, 1 NC) is nicknamed "Bon Gamin," which translates to English as the "good kid." And life is certainly well and good at the moment for the first French-born champion in UFC history as he enters his first full title defense on Saturday at UFC 334 against brash upstart Josh Hokit (10-0) in the main event at Madison Square Garden. No, Gane didn't become the undisputed champion in the traditional way, which makes his current title reign very much disputed to some. Injuries and multiple surgeries on both eyes forced Tom Aspinall to vacate the title after his fight with Gane ended in a no contest last October due to accidental eye pokes. Sign up for Paramount+ and watch UFC 334 for no additional fee -- every UFC numbered event and UFC Fight Night is included with your subscription! Plans start as low as $8.99/month or $89.99/year!
Gane was previously 0-for-2 in heavyweight title bouts thanks to disappointing losses to Francis Ngannou in 2022 and Jon Jones in 20203. But after he finished Alex Pereira via 2nd-round TKO in June at the White House to win the interim title – despite claims from the former two-division champion that he was repeatedly hit  behind the head – Gane was upgraded to full champion in September. 
        
            
                UFC 334 fight card -- Ciryl Gane vs. Josh Hokit: Five biggest storylines to follow in New York
                
                    Brian Campbell                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
From Gane's standpoint, whether it be defending himself against the sophomoric attempts from Hokit to get inside his head or the criticism of the public, he's far too blessed to be stressed. "I'm comfortable in this situation," Gane told CBS Sports on Tuesday. "I'm too happy, I'm too full of love. It doesn't matter if people want to talk about me the wrong way. That's OK. I'm happy. I'm with my friends. We are together in New York. We are going to fight. I'm healthy. I try to keep my family healthy, too. I'm OK." 
Gane's many vocal critics, whether it be fans or opposing fighters, tell a somewhat different story, however. If there's an elephant in the room surrounding Gane, it's the narrative that he's a dirty fighter. And it isn't just the results of his last two fights. In fact, all six of Gane's most recent UFC opponents dating back to 2022 have complained publicly about his conduct, from Alexander Volkov and Serghei Spivac to Jones and Tai Tuivasa. Even though Gane carries himself with such an amiable personality, it's hard to ignore his recent history, which raises an all-important question regarding intent.
"What he's doing in these fights is dirty, for sure. Obviously, all of these things are illegal," UFC legend and Paramount+ analyst Dustin Poirier told CBS Sports from the set of "Deep Waters" on Monday. "The question is: Is he intentionally going into these fights trying to get the upperhand? I don't know if that's the case … but it doesn't seem like he's trying to fix the problems or fix the illegal things that are happening because it keeps happening."For the record, veteran referee Herb Dean, who officiated Gane's UFC Freedom 250 win over Pereira, posted a video on social media defending Gane's strikes as legal under the unified rules and further explained that shots to the back of the head are only illegal when they connect with the nape of the neck. Pereira, however, in the aftermath of the loss, simply wouldn't let the topic go and has repeatedly taken shots at both Gane and Dean. 
"[Pereira] can do whatever he wants," Gane said. "People like to say some stupid things [about] me. But, it's just about statistics, just about the rules [and] the facts when the biggest referee in the history of the UFC is going to tell you, 'No, there is nothing special [or illegal] with Ciryl.' But the people like to talk. That's OK." Gane's trainer, Fernand Lopez, insists that his camp at the MMA Factory in Paris strictly impresses upon his fighters the dangers of not being in control. If an accidental foul happens during sparring, Lopez said he immediately halts the action to teach and impress upon it."I don't think [Gane's reputation] is something that is relevant, to be honest with you," Lopez told CBS Sports on Tuesday. "We live in a sport that has rules. You can't complain about rules when you don't listen to what the referee says to you. The referee, who has [worked] 3,000 matches is saying to you that this isn't a foul in the back of the head and then you keep saying to the other guys, 'You fouled me.' You are not respecting a referee. You are a fighter, you are not a referee. Why should I believe you?
"This is stupid to just listen to people online saying things because, then, things change. The same guy that is happy for the enforcement of the rules will be crying tomorrow."Lopez's comments, when applied to the Pereira fight only, are certainly reasonable and justified, especially given Dean's analysis. But Gane's history goes well beyond that, including the accidental use of illegal knees and elbows, along with groin shots. So, should Gane be considered more physically reckless than dirty? "I'm not saying [these allegations] are coming out of nowhere. People can be reckless, [Gane] might be reckless," Lopez said. "But it can happen to anyone [and] if experts stop listening to facts because they are disappointed in the losing fighter, that [changes everything]."
While Poirier believes Gane needs to become better at being in control of his physical weapons, he does, as a former fighter, have sympathy for how quickly the sport moves and the emotions that come with that. "It's hard to walk the line when you're in a scramble," Poirier said. "Shots are being fired, you're in a shootout and you're trying to hurt the guy. Things are going to happen. Eyes are going to get poked. Punches are going to land behind the ear and kind of behind the head when you're fighting like that. You are doing anything you can to hurt the person in front of you. But once it happens, there shouldn't be any more follow up shots. Once you do throw one or two and you realize what you're hitting, you shouldn't continue hitting that same spot."Poirier has plenty of history being on the wrong end what he believes are dirty tactics, from his heated 2022 win over Michael Chandler where he accused his opponent of putting fingers in his mouth and blowing bloody snot at him, along with multiple illegal strikes, to his trilogy with Conor McGregor that featured multiple accusations against the Irish superstar who Poirier labeled "a dirtbag." 
But it was Poirier's two-fight series with Eddie Alvarez in 2017 and 2018 where he learned firsthand the dangers of how an illegal strike can affect the momentum of a fight. Their first meeting at UFC 211 was ruled a no contest after Alvarez landed an illegal knee to the head of a downed opponent. Poirier won the rematch via 2nd-round TKO. "It was one of the worst concussion symptoms that I have had after a fight and I have been in some bangers," Poirier said. "It didn't seem crazy in the moment but it messed me up. The referee was saying it's hard to tell if [Alvarez] knew I was down and threw the knee illegally with intent. We will never know that. We can't get into a guy's head. There needs to be some kind of chain of command where we can go to instant replay or two people sitting side-by-side to review things. These things not only alter the fight, these alter people's careers. "It's a huge thing when these things don't get called or get called wrong."
Poirier believes the onus is on a fighter and his team, should they expect an opponent to be dirty, to plant a seed in the referee's mind during the pre-fight instructions in the locker room. More importantly, Poirier said he has always been against the idea of immediate retaliation to a foul as some form of street justice, mostly because of the importance for a fighter to remain as calm as possible and stick to the gameplan without letting emotions take over. 
When asked whether he believes Gane is a dirty fighter or whether the topic has played a role in his preparation, Hokit was immediately dismissive of it all, saying, "It doesn't matter." He did, however, add that he's prepared to retaliate immediately should anything happen on Saturday. "I don't even want to put too much thought into it but my thing is, if he hits me in the back of the head, I'm poking him in the eyes," Hokit said. "If he pokes me in the eyes, I hit him low. He hits me low, I've got to stab him now. He stabs me, I'm shooting him. He shoots me, I'm finding his family and killing them. He finds my family and kills them, I've got to go to France and I'm conquering his whole f---ing country. That's the mentality I bring."I'm not worried about it too much. I think it's all a part of fighting. If he pokes me in the eye, it is what it is. I'll fight blind, I don't care."
At the end of the day, Gane believes that the people in the fight game that truly matters -- his peers -- all understand what type of fighter and person he truly is at heart and that he has already moved on. "More and more now [I hear about this narrative] with my team because I'm not too focused on the social media," Gane said. "More and more you can see the real champions and the real good fighters saying, 'No, Cyril is not a cheater.' So, step by step, the people try to balance [it] a little bit. But I'm OK. It doesn't matter if people want to talk about me the wrong way. That's OK, that's OK."

title: What will PGA Tour do with Jon Rahm? How will DP World Tour playoffs shake out? - CBS Sports
description: CBS Sports' golf experts tackle the biggest questions in the sport with the inaugural edition of The Three Putt
body:
CBS Sports' golf experts tackle the biggest questions in the sport with the inaugural edition of The Three Putt
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:46 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        While the PGA Tour is in the midst of the FedEx Cup Fall, questions have emerged over the last couple of months from other pockets of the golf world. LIV Golf continues to navigate its bankruptcy process, which is expected to conclude with a league liquidation in early 2027, while the DP World Tour heads to Dubai to wrap up its postseason.At the center of both is Jon Rahm, who remains one of the best golfers in the world even if he has played fewer tournaments of consequence over the last couple of years. What, exactly, will Rahm do now that LIV Golf has shuttered and he has negotiated a release from his contract?As for the women's game, it continues to saunter on with WTGL being introduced to audiences this past weekend as its inaugural season commenced.The game keeps moving, and CBS Sports is keeping up with it as we dive into the most pressing issues and conversation points with the inaugural edition of The Three Putt.
Rahm finds himself eligible to play on the DP World Tour in 2027, but he has expressed an openness to returning to the PGA Tour and even accepting some penalties should an offer materialize from CEO Brian Rolapp and other key parties. If you were manning the PGA Tour, how would you handle Rahm and his status entering next season?Robby Kalland: I'm offering him a similar, but more expensive, version of the deal Brooks Koepka took (which Rahm and others declined). Rahm famously waited until LIV Golf made him an offer he felt he couldn't refuse, and while he's going to miss out on a considerable sum of that money after the league's bankruptcy, the financial penalty (charitable donation) to return should exceed the $5 million Koepka had to pay. I would double it to $10 million so Rahm could prove allegiance to the Tour and membership he turend his back on. Beyond that, I would keep the general structure -- forfeiting five years of eligibility for the Player Equity Program and missing out on 2027 FedEx Cup bonus payouts.Forcing Rahm to play on the DP World Tour, which is still something of a competitor even with the strategic alliance, for a year is not in the best interests of the PGA Tour. All parties will realize it's best to find a path back to the PGA Tour. What would be your ideal agreement in this scenario? 
Patrick McDonald: I'm bringing him back, too, and as you said, both sides are incentivized to reach a deal. It won't be as straightforward as Koepka (if we want to call that straightforward) since Rahm is eligible for signature events via the Official World Golf Rankings as of now, and the FedEx Cup is coming to an end after 2027, but the executives are making enough money to hash all the details out to appease the membership while penalizing Rahm. It should be noted what the start of the PGA Tour schedule means to Rahm, a former winner at The American Express and the Genesis Invitational. He also has connections to both Torrey Pines and the Scottsdale area, where he and his family of six reside.Kalland: I'll also make one final note on the appeasing membership point. Rolapp understands fully that not everyone is created equal in the PGA Tour hierarchy. While Rahm learned the hard way -- when he jumped ship for LIV Golf -- that he's not the needle mover he thought he might be, he's still worthy of having a door opened for him, whether that's fair or not. There will be some who cry foul, but as you noted, he's still high enough in the rankings to qualify for the top events on merit without having to really bend any rules. McDonald: Golfers, crying?! Never.Let's shift gears, considering the DP World Tour is about to end its season. Rahmbo is up to No. 11 in the Race to Dubai standings after his win in Abu Dhabi. Another LIV Golf alumnus, Eugenio Chacarra, is leading the season-long race with Rory McIlroy eyeing his eighth Race to Dubai belt and Patrick Reed rounding out the top three. What are you looking forward to the most?
Kalland: I want to see if Chacarra can fend off Reed, McIlroy and the rest. He's been electric this year, establishing himself as a star on the DP World Tour with three wins and four other top-3 finishes after a relatively quiet final couple of seasons on LIV Golf. For American golf fans, he's a lock to earn his PGA Tour card through the Race to Dubai rankings, and this will be a chance to get familiar with a guy who could come out swinging on the Tour in 2027. We're going to get to see him under some serious pressure from the world's best in Dubai, and I'm hoping he affirms his spot as a rising star. What's got your attention?McDonald: Chacarra's play and charisma have brought the term "swashbuckler" back into my lexicon, so I thank him for that. I'm glad you said "attention," because -- not to bring politics into it (which I would never, ever do) -- it's kind of crazy that this thing is being played given the current state of affairs in the region. I am just hoping we get some more uninterrupted golf under our belts. Rahm winning in Abu Dhabi and having a legit shot at taking home the Race to Dubai is equal parts hilarious and impressive. I hope he takes it home given his recent financial heartaches in court.
Kalland: Agreed. If we get another tournament completed and someone's lifting that gigantic Race to Dubai trophy at the end, it'll feel like a minor miracle.
WTGL kicked off (teed off?) last Sunday with a classic Los Angeles vs. New York rivalry that featured the return of Michelle Wie West against Lydia Ko and Rose Zhang. What are your expectations for WTGL's inaugural season, and will it ultimately be successful? What would you define as success for the new indoor league? McDonald: Believe it or not, I was boots on the ground synthetic turf last Sunday. My Steelers were on a bye, so I was hard at work inside the belly of the beast that is the SoFi Center. I couldn't believe this started on Sunday at 3 p.m. ET. Who decided that was a good idea to debut the league in the middle of an NFL Sunday? WTGL has four matches this year scheduled on the ABC family of networks, and all four are going against the NFL. It doesn't take an expert to know that eyeballs will be elsewhere. My expectations are low, and success might be as simple as somehow introducing one or two new personalities for LPGA fans to latch onto. Is that too harsh?Kalland: No. That's probably what the goal should be. Not to get too into the weeds on TV programming, but it is quite common for them to counterprogram the NFL with women's sports (WNBA, NWSL, women's college basketball). I presume the assumption is that the Venn diagram with the NFL has the least overlap there.
That said, it does limit your reach to find new fans if your broadcasts are all up against the NFL. The best part of TGL has been getting to see more of the personalities of PGA Tour players: some shining and others … not. I expect WTGL to be the same. If this can create a viral moment or two and let a few personalities shine that fans can latch on to beyond Nelly Korda, that's probably a win for women's golf, even if I don't see this being a real game changer for the sport.

title: Astros name franchise icon Brad Ausmus as new manager as Houston tries to turn back the clock - CBS Sports
description: Ausmus, who most recently served as the Yankees' bench coach, has five seasons of managerial experience under his
body:
Ausmus, who most recently served as the Yankees' bench coach, has five seasons of managerial experience under his belt
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:28 am ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Houston Astros have chosen Brad Ausmus as their next manager, the team announced on WednesdayAusmus replaces Joe Espada, whose contract as Houston manager was not renewed after three seasons. Espada led the Astros to the playoffs in two of those seasons."I am very excited to be back in Houston," Ausmus said in a statement. "The Astros and the city of Houston have been a huge part of my life, and I'm thrilled to create a new chapter as the team's manager. I'd like to thank [general manager Randy Flores] and the entire Astros organization for this opportunity, and I can't wait to get to work."Ausmus, 57, had served as bench coach for the New York Yankees since late 2023. Prior to that, he had two stints as a big-league manager. He first managed the Detroit Tigers from 2014-17, and over that span he guided the team to a 314-332 record and a division title in his first season. Ausmus also managed the Angels to a 72-90 record in 2019. Overall, Ausmus as a manager has a winning percentage of .478 in five seasons. Before his dugout career, Ausmus was a top defensive catcher for years. Ausmus's playing career spanned parts of 18 seasons in Major League Baseball, 10 of which came with the Astros. Along the way, Ausmus won three Gold Gloves behind the mask and earned an All-Star selection as a member of the Tigers in 1999. 
"We are thrilled to welcome Brad back to the Astros organization," Flores said in a statement. "Brad impressed us throughout the interview process, demonstrating the leadership, energy, and expertise critical to driving a winning culture both on and off the field. I am excited to work alongside Brad and happy to have him back in an Astros uniform."With Houston, Ausmus is the first major hire undertaken by Flores, who himself was named to his post earlier in the offseason. The Astros are coming off a division title and a postseason berth in 2026. However, they also finished 81-81 and had a negative run differential. It's an uncertain future, as the Astros have an aging roster in spots, a weak farm system, and multiple core contributors entering their walk years in 2027.It remains to be seen whether owner Jim Crane will try to wring out another season of contention from the roster or lean into a rebuild. Whatever the course, Ausmus will help guide it in a city where he remains a highly popular figure. 
As of Houston's decision to hire Ausmus, the Los Angeles Angels are the only team with a current managerial vacancy. Earlier in the offseason, the Philadelphia Phillies retained interim manager Don Mattingly on a permanent basis, as did the New York Mets with Andy Green, and the Seattle Mariners replaced Dan Wilson with Jason Kanzler.

title: MLB rumors: Yankees eye Alec Bohm, Tarik Skubal books more meetings, plus Nationals, Orioles, Mariners, more - CBS Sports
description: Here are your hot stove rumors for Wednesday, Nov. 11
body:
Here are your hot stove rumors for Wednesday, Nov. 11
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:40 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway. The ongoing CBA negotiations and the near certainty of an owner-implemented lockout on Dec. 1 loom over all, and it may indeed mean a flurry of trades and free agent signings leading up to that date. That was certainly the case leading up to the last lockout of 2021-22. As for the present moment, the General Manager Meetings in Las Vegas are underway, and since there may not be any Winter Meetings this offseason (thanks to the lockout), the GMs' pow-wow could instead be a locus of activity. Thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace and the ongoing GM Meetings, offseason rumors are flowing. Speaking of which, we'll be here each day to round up what's out there. You can find Wednesday's supply just below. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Yankees interested in Bohm
The New York Yankees are eyeing an upgrade at third base given the prolonged struggles of Ryan McMahon, and free agent Alec Bohm may be a potential target for GM Brian Cashman, according to the New York Post. Bohm, 30, is coming off a subpar walk year for the Philadelphia Phillies, but he has a career OPS+ of 101 overall. He also fared much better in the second half, and his season-long numbers were dragged down by a terrible April. Bohm is not much of a fielder these days, but the Yankees may be willing to live with that if they determine he can provide an offensive upgrade.As for McMahon, Cashman already conceded to looking for a replacement."He's signed through next year for us, but I definitely know we need to improve production in a lot of different spots on the club if we can," he told reporters on Tuesday. "So we'll be open-minded to finding what we can run into if it's there."
Skubal market continues to take shape
The market for ace Tarik Skubal, far and away the top free agent available this offseason, continues to pick up steam, and it may be that he signs his next contract before the owners lock out the players on Dec. 1. The Los Angeles Dodgers, who traded for Skubal leading up to the deadline, the New York Mets, the Chicago Cubs, and the San Diego Padres are known to have varying levels of interest in Skubal. Now, the New York Post reports, the Toronto Blue Jays have entered the fray and emerged as Skubal suitors. As for the Dodgers, they indeed plan to meet with Skubal, GM Brandon Gomes said. There could be a twist in their pursuit, though; The Athletic reports that the Dodgers are interested in Skubal on a short-term deal, presumably with a higher AAV like they gave to Kyle Tucker. But given the uncertainty of the CBA, would Skubal be willing to sign a contract that has him back on the market in just a few years?Mets top executive David Stearns, meanwhile, emphasized on Tuesday that he and the club are willing to offer lengthy contracts to pitchers but that circumstances matter. That, in theory, should allay fears that he's not prepared to make a significant offer.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Padres hoping for Pivetta reunion
The San Diego Padres not long ago declined their club option on right-handed starter Nick Pivetta. However, they may not mean a parting of ways for club and player. Padres lead decision-maker AJ Preller on Tuesday told reporters, including Marty Caswell, that the team hopes to work out a new agreement with Pivetta so that he can return to San Diego for the 2027 season and perhaps beyond. Pivetta enjoyed a standout season in 2025, but his 2026, while excellent while on the mound, consisted of just eight regular-season starts because of elbow problems. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Nationals getting trade interest in Dylan Crews
Dylan Crews, the 24-year-old outfielder for the Washington Nationals, has yet to reach the potential that made him the No. 2 overall draft pick in 2023. However, that ceiling is still there, and Crews is obviously young enough to realize his promise. Speaking of Crews, the Athletic reports that multiple teams have approached the Nats about Crews' availability in trade and that the Nats have not declared him off-limits. That of course doesn't mean a trade will happen, but a change of scenery for Crews may indeed be a winter possibility. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Mariners favoring Suzuki over Arozarena reunionOutfielder Randy Arozarena was the Seattle Mariners' top player last season, and now he's a free agent. The M's, though, may not be interested in bringing back Arozarena and instead may be targeting fellow free agent outfielder Seiya Suzuki, the Seattle Times reports. Each veteran outfielder will be going into his age-32 season in 2027, and each produced at a high level in 2026. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Orioles not inclined to tear it downAfter missing the playoffs in back-to-back seasons and trading away catcher Adley Rutschman leading up to the 2026 deadline, the Baltimore Orioles seem like a teardown candidate on paper. However, president of baseball operations Mike Elias batted down talk of a major roster makeover. "A lot of our key, core players are very unlikely to go anywhere," Elias told the media, including the Baltimore Banner, at the GM Meetings. That presumably means that coveted shortstop Gunnar Henderson, among other notable names, won't be going anywhere this winter.

title: Kirk Cousins traded to Vikings: Raiders gave QB option to stay or leave franchise, per report - CBS Sports
description: Minnesota gave up a third round pick to bring back Cousins
body:
Minnesota gave up a third round pick to bring back Cousins
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:21 am ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Maybe the most consequential trade of deadline day in the NFL wasn't actually made by a front office executive. Instead, the lone player in the deal gave it the final go-ahead. In the final hours before Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET deadline, the Minnesota Vikings pulled off a trade for Kirk Cousins, sending the Las Vegas Raiders a 2027 third-round pick to reunite with their former quarterback. Before ultimately agreeing to the deal, however, the Raiders put the ball in Cousins' court, according to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero. Las Vegas gave Cousins the chance to decide whether he'd like to leave the organization and head back to Minnesota or stay with the club he had started the first nine games of the 2026 season for. After talking with his family, agent Mike McCartney, and Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell, Cousins made up his mind by midday Tuesday and ultimately informed Raiders GM John Spytek that he wanted to return to Minnesota. Thus, the trade was made. "So much respect for John Spytek and the Raiders organization," McCartney told The Ringer's Tom Pelissero about how the team handled this trade. "There aren't many leaders in this league who would've done that. Very appreciative of Spy."
Part of the calculus in Cousins' decision to opt for a return to the Vikings was the presence of Fernando Mendoza. The report indicates Cousins knew it was only a matter of time before the Raiders turned the keys to the franchise over to the 2026 No. 1 overall pick, so his status as QB1 was fleeting. With an opportunity to go back and help a Vikings team he spent six years with and won the NFC North with in 2022, the proper pieces fell into place to give the deal the green light. This is also a pretty unprecedented move, as Cousins has the most single-season passing touchdowns (20) -- as well as career passing touchdowns (318) -- by any quarterback changing teams midseason in NFL history. 
During his first six-season stint with the Vikings, Cousins was second in the league in completiion percentage (67.9%), fourth in passing yards (23,265), and third in passing touchdowns (171) among all quarterbacks over that span with at least 50 starts. He also reunites with wide receiver Justin Jefferson, who averaged 98.9 receiving yards per game with Cousins -- an NFL record for most receiving yards by a quarterback-receiver duo over at least 50 games. While the 15-year veteran is now returning at 38, the hope is that he can come close to that production and give an offense tied for the fewest offensive touchdowns (11) in the NFL this season a boost.

        Former UFC bantamweight champion Merab Dvalishvili is accusing Usman Nurmagomedov and others of assaulting him and his friend during an RAF media event in Abu Dhabi.Ilia Topuria, the former two-division UFC champion, uploaded a video from the moment Dvalishvili was attacked."You're a bunch of cowards, and you'll be held accountable for what you've done," Topuria captioned the video. "You're anything but real men."
Dvalishvili posted a video on Wednesday while being attended to by medical professionals. Dvalishvili claimed that he and his friend, who were both visibly bloodied and bruised in the video, were jumped by Usman Nurmagomedov's team while promoting Real American Freestyle.
"What a sneaky way, guys. Just two of us, me and my friend, came here in Abu Dhabi, and Usman Nurmagomedov and his friends came like snakes from behind," Dvalishvili said in the video. "What kind of fighters you guys are? What kind of man does this, bro? If you want to fight, let's do it like the real way. You came just because there's the two of us? What the f---?"We bleed, we fight, we war, but you guys are just sneaky guys. You're not real men. It shows you guys' character. It shows you're not real men. What the f---, guys? If you want to fight, fight. Let's f---ing fight, we are fighters, bro. I'm a real guy, I talk shit, but you guys came from behind, bro. I don't know how many guys you were. All your friends waiting for us in a sneaky way. Wow. I knew what kind of guys you are. I came here in Abu Dhabi and Usman, Umar and his friends came in a sneaky way, so many guys."Dvalishvili elaborated on the incident in a written post on social media. Dvalishvili claimed that they were attacked from behind mid-interview, and that multiple people held them down while others struck them.
"[I] was doing an interview for RAF in hotel lobby and Usman and his buddies came up from behind and started punching me and my young friend," Dvalishvili wrote. "Security was holding me -- they kept kicking us when we were down like losers."Dvalishvili insisted that he was fine, while lamenting his alleged attackers' cowardly methods."I'm fine, guys, all my friends and family, I'm fine," he said in the video. "I'm a f---ng fighter."
"We were fighting like real men and you guys was fighting like pussies. Pussies does this bro. We were down and you were kicking us? Pussy guys. Pussy. We are warriors, bro."Dvalishvili and Umar Nurmagomedov have been tense since the lead-up to their January 2025 fight. Dvalishvili, the UFC bantamweight champion at the time, successfully defended the title via unanimous decision. Usman Nurmagomedov is a free agent who was recently signed to the Professional Fighters League and, before that, Bellator. He has been seen at recent UFC events.
The Nurmagomedov brothers are cousins and pupils of Khabib Nurmagomedov, the retired former UFC champion and UFC Hall of Famer. Khabib famously leaped into the crowd and attacked Dillon Danis moments after submitting Conor McGregor at UFC 229, inciting multi-man brawls inside and outside of the Octagon.

title: Predicting every College Football Playoff team's remaining schedule: Expect three-loss logjam in SEC - CBS Sports
description: SEC chaos will open the door for other CFP contenders down the stretch
body:
SEC chaos will open the door for other CFP contenders down the stretch
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:53 am ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The College Football Playoff committee revealed its latest bracket Tuesday, and 12 teams are in full control of their postseason fate. So, who is going to blow it?If you've been watching this sport for any length of time, you know the chances of every team in the field going 3-0 over the next three weeks are about as good as me stumbling across a winning lottery ticket on the sidewalk. Several teams in Tuesday night's CFP bracket will lose at least one game, and when that happens, other teams will be waiting to strike.According to CBS Sports' projections, five teams left out of the bracket on Tuesday still have at least a 1-in-5 shot to make the playoff. In the case of Wake Forest, its chances of reaching the field are far higher than not.Wake Forest -- 75.3%Texas Tech -- 48.4%Ohio State -- 36.7%Oregon -- 25.8%LSU -- 20.6%With the exception of LSU -- which plays No. 6 Texas and No. 8 Tennessee over the next two weeks -- most of those teams lack major resume-building opportunities down the stretch. That means they'll need some help, but the good news is they'll probably get it.

        
            
                College Football Playoff format for 24-team field: How rankings would look in 2026
                
                    Shehan Jeyarajah                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The SEC in particular could get chaotic between now and the end of the regular season, and I believe that the logjam of three-loss teams will only get bigger in that span. Should that happen, the Demon Deacons and Red Raiders could become the beneficiaries.With the final rankings reveal inching closer, here is how I see the rest of the season playing out for every College Football Playoff team.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    12. Boise State Projected remaining record: 3-0vs. Oregon State -- Wvs. San Diego State -- WTBD -- WThe duo of Braden Atkinson and Jesse Legree makes Oregon State a dangerous opponent, but the Broncos have been firing on all cylinders, regardless of who is at quarterback. Then I'm just not sure San Diego State has the requisite firepower to hang with Boise State for 60 minutes. Of course, the new Pac-12 is implementing the new FLEX game in the final week of the regular season, and Utah State is Boise State's projected opponent at the moment. The Broncos have already beaten the Aggies by 19.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    11. Kentucky Projected remaining record: 2-1vs. Florida -- Wat No. 22 Missouri -- Lvs. Louisville -- WComing off its loss to Tennessee, Kentucky must win out to remain in the College Football Playoff field. The Gators have 15 points in their last two games combined, and I don't see them suddenly snapping out of that funk against Kentucky. The trip to Missouri, on the other hand, is very dangerous. The Tigers have the passing attack to beat the Wildcats over the top, and I think that's what will happen. Listen, 9-3 with a win over Louisville to close things out would be a great start for the Will Stein era.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    10. BYU Projected remaining record: 3-0vs. Baylor -- Wat Kansas -- Wvs. Cincinnati -- WThe Cougars now have to peel themselves off the mat and power through the rest of the season without losing again. This weekend's game against Baylor will test their resolve, especially with how well DJ Lagway has been playing, but playing at home gives BYU enough of an edge that I'm not too worried. I'm not too worried about Kansas pulling an upset, and while Cincinnati has been feisty at times this season, that's a tough road trip for the Bearcats to make at the end of the season.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    9. Indiana Projected remaining record: 3-0vs. No. 18 USC -- Wat Washington -- Wvs. Purdue -- WBased on what we've seen from Indiana so far this season, it's hard to have much confidence in any of these picks, but the open date probably did come at the right time. Maybe Josh Hoover is healthier, and that will spark the offense. USC has the talent to win on Saturday, but the Trojans have been awful on the road in Big Ten play. See their loss to Wisconsin for an example. From there, the Hoosiers defense should be able to overpower Washington and Purdue, even if the offense isn't firing on all cylinders.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    8. Tennessee Projected remaining record: 2-1at Texas A&M -- Wvs. No. 21 LSU -- Lat Vanderbilt -- WThe Volunteers could go anywhere from 3-0 to 1-2 in the final three games, and none of those outcomes would surprise me. Tennessee has struggled on the road, so I picked them to beat Texas A&M with little confidence, although the matchup between the Vols defense and Aggies offense is incredibly lopsided. That would set up a monumental clash with Lane Kiffin and LSU in Neyland Stadium, and that's where Tennessee's offensive firepower finally becomes the Achilles heel.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    7. Miami Projected remaining record: 3-0vs. Duke -- Wvs. Virginia Tech -- Wvs. Boston College -- WYou really couldn't draw up the final three games any better than this if you're Miami. They're all at home against teams you'll be heavily favored against. Duke may want revenge for the Darian Mensah saga, but that doesn't mean the Blue Devils have the roster to get it. Virginia Tech could be tricky if Ethan Grunkemeyer plays well at quarterback, but the Hokies just got trounced by SMU. The Eagles will be nothing more than cannon fodder and an opportunity for Mensah to pad his stats for the Heisman Trophy race.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    6. Texas Projected remaining record: 2-1at No. 21 LSU -- Lvs. Arkansas -- Wat Texas A&M -- WThe Longhorns are going into Death Valley to face a desperate LSU team that's sitting on three losses already. That's a dangerous situation for Texas to walk into, and the Horns leave Baton Rouge with a loss. Arkansas is as good a rebound spot as you're going to find in the SEC, so that shouldn't be an issue for the Horns. Admittedly, Texas taking three losses into College Station is a risky proposition, but Texas A&M may already have seven losses by that point.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    5. Notre Dame Projected remaining record: 3-0vs. Boston College -- Wvs. SMU -- Wat Syracuse -- WI would say Notre Dame is poised for a letdown performance, but I'm not sure Boston College could take advantage of it, even if the Fighting Irish do come out flat. As for Syracuse, I know SMU has already fallen victim to the JMA Wireless Dome magic, but the Orange will be greatly out-matched in the regular-season finale. That leaves the Mustangs as the only real threat to Notre Dame, and even that is a stretch. Kevin Jennings will need to play the best game of his career if SMU is going to pull the upset.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    4. UCLA Projected remaining record: 2-1vs. Illinois -- Wat Michigan -- Lvs. No. 18 USC -- WCall me a hater or a doubter, but I don't see UCLA running the table in the regular season. That means the Bruins will have to lose one of their last three games. It's just a matter of figuring out which one. Ultimately, Michigan was the choice for a few reasons. The travel and weather could be brutal at that time of year, and the Wolverines defense is capable of making Ty Dieffenbach uncomfortable. USC is another potential loss, but Bob Chesney will have his team ready to go in a big rivalry matchup against the Trojans.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    3. Alabama Projected remaining record: 3-0at Vanderbilt -- Wvs. Chattanooga -- Wvs. Auburn -- WAlabama has the easiest road to the finish line of any team currently in the College Football Playoff field, which is why that win over LSU was so huge. The Crimson Tide can get away with their "C" game against Vanderbilt and Chattanooga, with all due respect to the Commodores and Mocs. description: With this being the last ride for conference championship games, Week 11's college football slate will make the race to get there worth
body:
With this being the last ride for conference championship games, Week 11's college football slate will make the race to get there worth watching. There are seismic matchups in every Power Four league this weekend, and the fallout could reach beyond the league standings with the College Football Playoff picture continuing to take shape. Multi-loss teams needing to win out, along with favorites hoping to remain out front, spike the conversation, with heavy stakes surrounding USC-Indiana, Wake Forest-SMU and Texas-LSU, among others.These picks have been tricky all season, but most of the lines are even tighter this week.Season results: Brad Crawford (59-31 straight up, 42-47-1 ATS); Chris Hummer (64-26 straight up, 46–43-1 ATS)
Not throwing in the towel yet this season, but man, I'm frustrated. Last week's all-time weekend of games generated a nauseating 3-6 finish ATS while Hummer strengthened his lead at 5-4 entering Week 11. Alabama's win over LSU was special for the Crimson Tide, who hadn't been all that convincing recently despite early love from the CFP selection committee. And I never saw Oregon's destruction of Ohio State coming -- neither of us did.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 13 Wake Forest (-1.5) at SMUHummer (Wake Forest -1.5): This game is going to come down to which defense. These are two top 10 passing offenses in the FBS, averaging more than 300 yards per game each. It's how the two teams win. The big advantage for the Demon Deacons is their run defense. They're top 10 nationally in that category and should be able to generally mitigate a very up-and-down SMU rushing attack. 
The Wake Forest secondary can be an occasional liability. But the Demon Deacons have the advantage of basically coming off a bye (Merrimack). I like them to go on the road and make a statement. … Wake Forest 38, SMU 34.Crawford (Wake Forest -1.5): The Demon Deacons are just obliterating teams in the ACC this season since that early-September loss to Miami. Jake Dickert's proving a point, and his comments associated with the end of league championship weekend were quite revealing -- he wants to win a conference title and must go through Dallas to do it. By winning out, Wake Forest will get its rematch with Miami. I think it's going to happen as long as the Demon Deacons can get a couple stops this weekend. ... Wake Forest 41, SMU 31.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Duke at No. 7 Miami (-13.5)Hummer (Miami -13.5): There's a lot of interconnectivity in this game. Not only was Manny Diaz the one-time head coach of the Hurricanes, but Miami's star quarterback (Darian Mensah) and wide receiver (Cooper Barkate) both came from Duke this offseason in somewhat controversial fashion. It could be difficult for Miami to get up for this game a week after Notre Dame. But considering the loss and the ties between the two schools, I expect Miami to be all in. Duke plays slow and controls the pace of games with an excellent defense and a strong run game. But Miami is the nation's best rushing defense, and the Hurricanes have the firepower to separate down the stretch. … Miami 31, Duke 17.
Crawford (Miami -13.5): I haven't downgraded the Hurricanes as a national championship contender, nor should you this season. As long as Malachi Toney returns for the ACC Championship in a couple of weeks, this team will be fine. He's such a huge part of Shannon Dawson's offense that it simply was going to take several series to figure out last week at Notre Dame and when Miami did, the offense produced. Miami's rush defense is one of the best in the country, and they're going up against the potential Doak Walker winner in Nate Sheppard. Be careful in this spot. ... Miami 30, Duke 14.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Northwestern at No. 20 Ohio State (-10.5)Hummer (Ohio State -10.5): There's been a lot of noise around Ohio State this week. Those are fair critiques, and the Wildcats are a very dangerous team if Aidan Chiles is healthy. But I just expect the Buckeyes to respond. The Wildcats have struggled defensively this season, especially against the run, and that could open things up for Ohio State's offense even with a freshman QB. And as good as Chip Kelly is as a playcaller, this is by far the best defense the Wildcats have seen since Indiana. Give me the Buckeyes to cover. … Ohio State 31, Northwestern 20.
Crawford (Ohio State -10.5): Picking the Buckeyes to cover for a third straight week is worrying, especially when the last two plays haven't cashed. What has happened to this team under Ryan Day? Much of the finger-pointing should go to the defense, because there's an inherent built-in excuse when you lose your starting -- Heisman-caliber -- quarterback. Northwestern is a solid team and could certainly keep this under the number, but against my better judgment, I'll take Ohio State again. ... Ohio State 28, Northwestern 13.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 8 Tennessee (-2.5) at Texas A&MHummer (Tennessee -2.5): How is Texas A&M going to score against Tennessee? That's my big question going into this game. The Vols have a top 20 defense and one of the truly elite defensive fronts (4th nationally in pressure rate) in the sport. That's a huge problem for an Aggies front that's struggled at times this season and a quarterback in Marcel Reed who's struggled with consistency. 
Texas A&M's offense did look a bit better last week. It just failed to convert in the red zone. Maybe the Aggies find their stride. But I'd bet on the better, more consistent team. … Tennessee 24, Texas A&M 20.Crawford (Tennessee -2.5): This line's begging me to take the Aggies, but I do wonder where this team's head is at with four wins in nine games, needing two more just to reach bowl eligibility. Expect another low-scoring slugfest, determined by which team converts red-zone possessions into touchdowns. 
Texas A&M failed to do it at South Carolina and now takes on a higher-ranked opponent who had just lost to the Gamecocks before shellacking Kentucky. Vols win a close one, and Mike Elko fails to get Texas A&M to bowl season. Yikes. ... Tennessee 23, Texas A&M 20.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Michigan at No. 16 Oregon (-10.5)Hummer (Michigan +10.5): Can Michigan score? That's the big question entering this one. The Wolverines have only scored more than 21 points once this season against Power Four competition (Rutgers). Could that change after the firing of OC Jason Beck? 
It could. The same thing seemed to have worked for Oregon after firing Drew Mehringer, as the Ducks have averaged 37.5 points since the change. I don't see Michigan winning this game. But one thing I can count on with the Wolverines is their defense. That unit has kept them in every game this season. It does so again in Eugene. … Oregon 24, Michigan 17.Crawford (Oregon -10.5): Michigan's a mess right now, and Kyle Whittingham's comments about Oregon's NIL-infused roster are going to spike this one pre-game inside the Ducks' locker room.You just know Dan Lanning is going to super-size that soundbite. These are two teams trending in completely opposite directions, so the pick is to go with the squad with something to play for at Autzen Stadium. Oregon keeps pace in the CFP at-large discussion and pummels the Wolverines.  ... Oregon 27, Michigan 16.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 18 USC at No. 9 Indiana (-7.5)Hummer (Indiana -7.5): Both teams are coming off a bye and headed down the home stretch. This is yet another test for the Trojans in the ET time zone, a problem for Lincoln Riley since he arrived in Los Angeles. The Hoosiers are the nation's top-ranked defense and should be able to slow USC's passing attack. The question then becomes if a week off for Josh Hoover, who's dealt with a shoulder injury, can spark a struggling Indiana offense, which hasn't cleared the 20-point barrier in regulation since Oct. 3. The Trojans' defense, which ranks 88th nationally, is often a salve for opposing offenses. … Indiana 28, USC 20.Crawford (USC +7.5): College football's game-of-the-week in my eyes; I love the resiliency USC has shown this season. From losing to Oregon at home to clubbing Ohio State in the same situation, credit Lincoln Riley for getting the Trojans ready to play. Now at 7-2 overall, every goal is still ahead of USC coming down the stretch. Indiana has won so many close games, including a pair in overtime, and this one might go to an extra session, too. ... Indiana 27, USC 23.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 22 Missouri at No. 1 Georgia (-15.5)Hummer (Missouri +15.5): I'd pick Georgia over anyone right now. The Bulldogs are playing that well. But that's a big line against a Missouri team that's playing really good football. The Tigers are going to score with Austin Simmons under center, and their defense is still a top 30 unit nationally. Georgia wins, but Missouri keeps it close enough. … Georgia 34, Missouri 21.Crawford (Missouri +15.5): If the Georgia team that clapped Ole Miss shows up the rest of the season, Kirby Smart is going to win his third national championship. The Bulldogs were ferocious on the road and will have to do it again next week at a hostile South Carolina. However, this one can't be overlooked. The transitive property would suggest another blowout considering Ole Miss trounced Missouri by 28 points previously, but I'm going with a late touchdown spoiling Georgia's cover. ... Georgia 27, Missouri 17.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Florida at No. 11 Kentucky (-3.5)Hummer (Kentucky -3.5): The Gators' offense was the storyline of college football through four weeks. It's largely collapsed, averaging a total of 7.5 points over the last two weeks. The good news is Florida gets to play Kentucky (61st nationally in yards allowed per play) instead of Georgia or Oklahoma, but it will still be a challenge. The Wildcats have a big advantage in this game with their offensive front. I expect them to run the ball well against Florida and make the plays late when it matters. … Kentucky 21, Florida 17.Crawford (Kentucky -3.5): Our analytics model at CBS Sports suggests the Wildcats have a mere 11% chance to reach the CFP after last week's loss at Tennessee. However, I'm projecting the Wildcats to win out and get there with a 10-2 record. Nine wins isn't going to cut it when you consider Kentucky's resume, so Saturday's game against the Gators is a must-win. ... Kentucky 27, Florida 20.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 2 Utah (-2.5) at No. 23 ArizonaHummer (Utah -2.5): This is by far the toughest remaining game on Utah's schedule. The Wildcats are one of the top-scoring offenses in college football, and they're quietly a top-30 defense in terms of yards per play as well. What works in Utah's favor is excellent secondary play. The Utes are fifth nationally in opposing passer rating, and they should at least be able to slow Noah Fifita and Arizona's offense. Utah keeps its perfect season rolling for another week. … Utah 27, Arizona 24.Crawford (Utah -2.5): I've already penciled in Utah at12-0 entering conference championship weekend. The Utes have appeared flawless, sans a couple of possessions last week against BYU. Motivated by the allure of a first-round, the Utes will keep it going against the Wildcats. Hummer's right -- it's the toughest game left for the Utes and the only matchup standing between them and a potential unbeaten regular season. ... Utah 35, Arizona 31.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 6 Texas at No. 21 LSU (-3.5)Hummer (LSU -3.5): This is going to be a challenge for Texas. The Longhorn offensive line is banged up, and it's struggled to pass protect (94th nationally in pressure rate allowed in passing situations) while the Tigers have one of the best pass rush units in the FBS. Arch Manning will have to play clean and on time to help mitigate that advantage. Working in Texas' favor is one of the nation's best overall defenses, which will need to step up in the red zone where LSU has struggled this season. The Longhorns have played better of late. But Baton Rouge is arguably the toughest place to win in college football. LSU gets a win it desperately needs. … LSU 27, Texas 21.Crawford (LSU -3.5): Zero wins against ranked teams, and we're still talking about CFP hypotheticals for the Tigers with three games to play. Lane Kiffin hasn't figured it out yet against quality opponents, but perhaps that happens for the first time Saturday night against the Longhorns. Texas holds four ranked wins and doesn't need this one to reach the CFP as an at-large selection. With their backs against the wall, the Tigers get it done despite Sam Leavitt not playing turnover-free. ... LSU 30, Texas 24.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 12 Texas Tech at No. 25 Oklahoma State (-3.5)Hummer (Texas Tech +3.5): Given what we saw from Texas Tech's defense this week, this game could be yet another old-fashioned Big 12 shootout. The Cowboys have arguably the best quarterback in college football and the Big 12's top offense. Texas Tech, for its part, seems to have found its offensive rhythm with Thomas Castellanos under center. The big problem for both of these teams is slowing down the opposing pass game. But I do think the Red Raiders are the better defensive front seven. That makes the difference as Texas Tech ekes out a victory. … Texas Tech 35, Oklahoma State 34.Crawford (Oklahoma State -3.5): I'm not surprised the Cowboys are favored here. The numbers from Drew Mestemaker and Caleb Hawkins are impressive and after West Virginia's success last week against this Texas Tech defense, more fireworks are coming. Not only does Oklahoma State win, but the Cowboys cover and thwart Texas Tech's shot at getting back to the CFP. ... Oklahoma State 41, Texas Tech 35.

body:
The early signing day for the 2027 class opens on Wednesday, with six of the top 10 prospects remaining uncommitted
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:44 am ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The class of 2027's early signing period begins Wednesday. In an era where more and more ranked players are deciding early, National Signing Day itself has become a bit anticlimactic -- and, unlike football recruiting, where there can be some last-second fireworks, we aren't likely to see any last-minute flips or changes of heart to spice things up.Especially not with 127 of the 247Sports Top150 already committed.While the majority of the top players in the class have already made their decisions, six of the top 10 players in the class -- including top-ranked Beckham Black -- enter the week undecided.There was some juice over the last few weeks when North Carolina landed No. 4-ranked DeMarcus Henry, Villanova got a big commitment from No. 7-ranked Lewis Uvwo, and Will Wade got his first five-star back at LSU in the form of No. 9-ranked Reese Alston. No. 10-ranked Jordan Page Is the other top 10 prospect committed, pledging to UConn back on Oct. 4.To get you ready for the next few weeks and the remainder of the 2027 cycle, here is a look at the top classes so far for this cycle, the status of the top uncommitted players in the 2027 class, along with some general recruiting storylines that we are following.
LSU, Duke headline 2027's top 10 basketball recruiting classesLeading the way as the week tips off is Will Wade. Back in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, where he once got fired, at least in part, for allegedly making a "strong-ass offer" to a potential recruit, Wade has put together one strong-ass early signing class that includes four of the nation's top 20 players.Who else is making noise at the beginning of the signing period? It is important to acknowledge that the days of programs regularly signing four, five and even six top-ranked players during the early period seem to be gone, so quality counts a lot more than quantity these days when it comes to assembling the top high school recruiting classes.Right now, LSU has the No. 1 class, followed by Duke and UConn. The Tigers have four commits, all in the top 20 of the 247Sports rankings --  Reese Alston (No. 9), King Gibson (No. 17), Ahmad Hudson (No. 18), Xavier Young (No. 20).
The Blue Devils are right behind LSU with three commitments and the No. 2-ranked class featuring Asa Montgomery (No. 14), Kager Knueppel (No. 16), and Luke Paul (four-star recruit).At No. 3 is UConn with Jordan Page (No. 10), Navorro Bowman Jr. (No. 11), and Keny Vado (four-star recruit) all committed.Here is a look at the complete class of 2027 team rankings so far for this cycle.
Status of top 10 prospects in 2027The nation's top two players, No. 1-ranked Beckham Black and No. 2-ranked CJ Rosser, are teammates at Orlando (Fla.) Southeastern Prep Academy. And while it looked like their recruitment and ultimate landing spot could be intertwined, it's looking more and more like they'll be making independent decisions.Both prospects have already visited Arkansas, North Carolina and USC.No. 1 - Beckham BlackThe skilled and aggressive floor general has also taken official visits to Florida, Georgetown and Texas during the process.At this point, there are a few major things we are watching. Will he visit Duke? Will he do so before the end of the early signing period? And will a Duke visit make a difference if he does?
Black has never really committed to a decision timeline, but there has been recent buzz that he could make his pick during the early period. Regardless of when he makes his pick, it is John Calipari and the Razorbacks who have been generating the most behind-the-scenes talk over the past few weeks.Beckham Black vs. Serbia's Matija Lukic at the FIBA U17 Basketball World Cup Final 
                                                                    Getty Images
                                                            No. 2 - CJ RosserRosse has also visitd Kentucky, Louisville, Miami and NC State.Home-state North Carolina has long been considered the favorite for the smooth face-up four man and, as of today, we would still give Michael Malone and the Heels the edge.Kentucky is thought to be picking up some steam lately, and there's also been some talk about Arkansas, but UNC continues to get the most chatter.
While Rosser has previously told 247Sports that he's planning to take additional unofficial visits during the season before making a decision, there is some smoke starting to blow suggesting that he's much closer to a choice.No. 3 - Cayden DaughtryWith visits to Arkansas, Florida, Florida State, Iowa, Louisville, Miami and Tennessee under his belt, Daughtry could switch things up and make a decision if he wanted to.However, we are still expecting him to sit out the early signing period and make a winter decision.
Iowa was thought to be the leader early in the process before a lot of talk circulated that he wouldn't leave the state of Florida.Now, after seemingly losing some steam, the Hawkeyes have been getting mentioned a bit more. At this point, it would be tough to call a leader in this one.
        
            
                Meet Cayden Daughtry, the hottest name in high school basketball, who rewrote Peach Jam's record books
                
                    Isaac Trotter                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
No. 5 - AJ WilliamsMany expected that Williams might have been off the board to BYU by now.The small forward from Georgia did see Auburn, Georgia and Mississippi State before his mid-October visit to BYU, but he's not taken any visits since, despite talk that he could see Arkansas or Kentucky.
Unless another visit materializes, we still like Kevin Young and the Cougars to add a five-star prospect for the fourth straight year. If a program is in position to throw a wrench into BYU's plans, it could be Georgia.No. 6 - Adan DiggsThe slick combo guard from Goodyear (Ariz.) Millennium is currently planning to reveal his decision next Monday, Nov. 16. He's down to home state Arizona, along with Arkansas, Kentucky and USC.Tommy Lloyd and the Wildcats have been considered the favorites for some time now.
No. 8 - Nasir AndersonAnderson is a big, athletic and physical point guard who took trips to Georgia, North Carolina, Providence, Tennessee and Virginia over the past few months.The last time we spoke with Anderson, he was leaning towards taking some time to make a choice, but Georgia (his home state), Tennessee and Virginia look to be in the best shape.We wouldn't be surprised if Anderson elected to take another visit or two, so until he says otherwise, we don't expect him to commit early.
Emergence of mid-major commitments One big trend in college basketball recruiting we have noticed over the last few years is the emergence of mid-major schools landing more and more top recruits. Of the top 150 prospects in the 2027 class, 28 of the 127 committed players are going to mid-majors. That's over 20%. 10 or 15 years ago, this would never have been the case. Almost the entire 150 would be going to Power Five schools. But now, if you look up and down the top 150 rankings, you see schools like Utah State, VCU, George Mason, Duquesne, UNLV, FAU, St. Mary's, San Diego State, USF, St. Joseph's, New Mexico, and Tennessee Tech with top 150 commitments. While it's not unusual to see schools like VCU or San Diego State get in the mix here, there is a growing trend of more and more mid-majors being able to land higher-ranked recruits.So why is this happening?The simple answer is because of the transfer portal. Power Five schools are taking fewer and fewer high school recruits. It makes more sense to get an experienced second- or third-year player from the transfer portal who can contribute immediately at the college level than to develop a freshman who is ranked outside the top 50. A veteran transfer with a few years of college experience will be able to contribute and impact winning a lot quicker than a college freshman. So because Power Five schools are taking fewer high school recruits, mid-major programs can swoop into the top 150 and land players. There is a money element at play as well.  Power Five schools spend so much on transfer players that there isn't enough cash for high school players outside the top 50. Mid-majors, especially those that don't have football programs, are able to offer competitive NIL packages to land these high school players.
