title: College Football QB Power Rankings: Gunner Stockton, CJ Carr rise entering Week 11 - CBS Sports
description: Gunner Stockton's performance in Georgia's 42-7 win at Ole Miss in Week 10 provided a reminder of just how dangerous the Bulldogs can be
body:
Gunner Stockton's performance in Georgia's 42-7 win at Ole Miss in Week 10 provided a reminder of just how dangerous the Bulldogs can be when they are clicking on all cylinders. With UGA's defense and run game also in prime form, the veteran quarterback produced a gem that showcased how well-rounded a player he's become.After a couple of lackluster performances against Auburn and Florida, Stockton delivered as both a runner and passer during the Bulldogs' authoritative romp. He flashed his arm strength on a pair of bombs to Talyn Taylor, showed his elusiveness on an improvisational third-quarter touchdown pass to Taylor and also used his wheels on a 15-yard touchdown run in the first half.Georgia would have won the game even with unremarkable quarterback play. But that won't always be the case if the Bulldogs are going to return to the top of college football for the first time since the 2022 season. Stockton will need to be at his best at some point(s) during the College Football Playoff, and his performance against Ole Miss offered a reminder of how good Stockton's best is.
He is on the rise in this week's QBPR. So is Notre Dame's CJ Carr, who led the Fighting Irish to a win over Miami after a couple of uncharacteristically inaccurate games. Elsewhere in the top 20, North Texas' Tayven Jackson is making an appearance, replacing BYU's Bear Bachmeier, who drops to No. 21.
We've pointed out Bachmeier's propensity for untimely interceptions in this space over the past few weeks. It really came back to bite him in BYU's 28-20 loss to Utah.Here is this week's full QBPR 1-50.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    1. Darian Mensah, MiamiMensah recovered from a slow start and put the Hurricanes in position to have a chance in their 31-24 loss at Notre Dame. Playing without top target Malachi Toney, he settled in against the best defense on Miami's schedule and threw three touchdowns. His lone interception late in the third quarter was a costly one, as it gave Notre Dame good field position for a touchdown drive. But his edge at No. 1 in the QBPR was significant, and it will take a lot to dislodge the nation's leader in passing efficiency. Last week: 1
                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. CJ Carr, Notre DameCarr turned in a gem while leading Notre Dame to a win over top-ranked Miami in Week 10, as he completed 29 of 40 passes for 319 yards and three touchdowns. It was his first 300-yard performance of the season, and it came in a must-win spot after a couple of unspectacular showings. After struggling on mid-to-deep throws against BYU and Navy, Carr completed 4 of 7 throws traveling 15+ air yards against the 'Canes. Last week: 6

                            
    
                                                
                    
    3. Gio Lopez, Wake ForestLopez didn't play in Wake Forest's 77-0 win over Merrimack as the Demon Deacons sat him for precautionary reasons in a game against an overmatched opponent. Snagging a week of rest for the star lefty ahead of this week's showdown at SMU was probably wise. Wake Forest is in position to reach the ACC title game and potentially the College Football Playoff because of how efficient the North Carolina transfer has been both as a passer (18 touchdowns and just one interception) and as a runner with six touchdowns on the ground. Last week: 2
                            
    
                                                
                    
    4. Drew Mestemaker, Oklahoma StateMestemaker turned in a vintage performance in Oklahoma State's 66-28 win at Kansas State, throwing for 313 yards and four touchdowns. He's now the national leader in passing touchdowns with 29 and is eighth in passer efficiency. The North Texas transfer has a showcase opportunity this week against Texas Tech. Last week: 4
                            
    
                                                
                    
    5. Keelon Russell, AlabamaAlabama spent most of its 31-13 win at LSU playing defense. But when Russell had the football, he did good things, completing 17 of 24 passes for 206 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions. The talented sophomore is second in the SEC in passer rating, yards per attempt and passing touchdowns. Last week: 9

                            
    
                                                
                    
    6. Gunner Stockton, GeorgiaFour of Stockton's nine completions went for touchdowns in Georgia's 42-7 rout of Ole Miss as the veteran got back on track by accounting for five total touchdowns. He leads the SEC in passing touchdowns (20), yards per attempt (9.5) and passer rating and may just reemerge in the Heisman discussion with a strong finish against Missouri, South Carolina and Georgia Tech. Last week: 17
                            
    
                                                
                    
    7. Devon Dampier, UtahDampier totaled 177 yards and two touchdowns as a passer, 89 yards and two touchdowns as a runner and 29 yards receiving in Utah's massive 28-20 win over rival BYU. Of Utah's 62 offensive plays, 47 were either a Dampier run, pass or reception. Though the Utes' offense suffered through a prolonged midgame lull, he started with a bang and then delivered with the game on the line. Last week: 20
                            
    
                                                
                    
    8. Jayden Maiava, USCBefore USC's Week 10 bye, Maiava completed 15 of 22 passes for 222 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions in a 30-18 upset win over Ohio State. Completions of 69 and 70 yards accounted for much of the production as Maiava and the Trojans rediscovered their explosiveness one week after getting shut down by Wisconsin. Last week: 7

                            
    
                                                
                    
    9. Conner Weigman, HoustonWeigman was his usual steady self in Houston's 31-24 win over Cincinnati, throwing two touchdowns and running for another. He's up to 22 touchdown passes against just two interceptions for the season. The former Texas A&M transfer is No. 11 nationally in EPA per dropback and has the Cougars firmly in the mix for consecutive 10-win seasons. Last week: 8
                            
    
                                                
                    
    10. Braden Atkinson, Oregon StateAtkinson became the first FBS quarterback to reach 3,000 passing yards in a 42-21 loss to Texas State, but it wasn't his finest performance. The Bobcats held Atkinson to a season-low 192 yards through the air as he completed just 20 of 36 passes with no touchdowns and an interception. It was the first time this season he's been held below 300 yards and without a touchdown. Last week: 3
                            
    
                                                
                    
    11. Noah Fifita, ArizonaFifita threw for 313 yards and two touchdowns while also rushing for another score in Arizona's Week 10 win over TCU. The fifth-year star ranks second in the Big 12 behind only Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker in passing yards with 2,794 heading into a marquee moment against Utah this week. Last week: 12

                            
    
                                                
                    
    12. Michael Hawkins Jr., West VirginiaPoor execution in the fourth quarter ruined an impressive West Virginia rally at Texas Tech. But Hawkins' raw statistical production continues to dazzle. He accounted for 391 total yards, including 303 passing yards on just 16 attempts, in the Mountaineers' 53-48 loss to the Red Raiders. He is No. 8 nationally in EPA per dropback and leads all quarterbacks with 19 rushing touchdowns. Last week: 14
                            
    
                                                
                    
    13. Aidan Chiles, NorthwesternChiles missed Iowa's 24-10 loss to Northwestern with an upper body injury. It's been a renaissance season for the Michigan State transfer, who ranks No. 15 nationally in both EPA per dropback and yards per attempt. Last week: 13
                            
    
                                                
                    
    14. Sam Leavitt, LSULeavitt threw for 380 yards in LSU's 31-13 loss to Alabama. But the Tigers repeatedly failed to execute in critical moments while squandering the chance for a much-needed marquee victory. The Arizona State transfer has been better in the season's second half, and he leads the SEC in passing yards (2,553). He still hasn't proven he can deliver in a tight game against a quality opponent. Last week: 15

                            
    
                                                
                    
    15. Trinidad Chambliss, Ole MissThere's no way to sugarcoat it. This has been a disappointing season for Chambliss, who was harassed all night while completing 18 of 34 passes for 170 yards with no touchdowns and an interception in Ole Miss' 42-7 Week 10 loss to Georgia. He's still been good, but meeting the standard he set during the Rebels' CFP semifinal run last season has proven tough. Last week: 5
                            
    
                                                
                    
    16. Lincoln Kienholz, LouisvilleKienholz's 11 rushing touchdowns are fifth nationally among quarterbacks, and he's up to No. 13 in EPA per dropback after another strong showing against Georgia Tech. The Ohio State transfer has quietly led the Cardinals to four straight wins. Last week: 16
                            
    
                                                
                    
    17. Kenny Minchey, KentuckyMinchey kept Kentucky in the game against Tennessee's swarming defense by completing 26 of 34 passes before the Volunteers finally pulled away in the fourth quarter. The Wildcats remain a perfect 7-0 this season in games when the Notre Dame transfer does not throw an interception. They are now 0-2 when he's picked off. Last week: 10

                            
    
                                                
                    
    18. LaNorris Sellers, South CarolinaSellers delivered a game-clinching 41-yard touchdown run with 1:19 remaining in South Carolina's 17-9 win over Texas A&M in Week 10. It was the Gamecocks' fourth straight win as Sellers' improved play has revitalized what once appeared like a lost season. Last week: 18
                            
    
                                                
                    
    19. Kevin Jennings, SMUJennings ranks No. 5 nationally in both passing yards (2,764) and passing touchdowns (25) after torching Virginia Tech for 350 yards and four touchdowns. Once viewed as a turnover liability, the fifth-year star has thrown just one interception over the Mustangs' last five games. Last week: 19
                            
    
                                                
                    
    20. Tayven Jackson, North TexasAfter a fifth straight 300+ yard passing performance in North Texas' 52-23 win over Rice, Jackson's body of work is impossible to ignore. The well-traveled fifth-year star is No. 3 nationally in passing yards (2,880), No. 3 in EPA per dropback, No. 7 in passer efficiency and No. 7 in passing touchdowns (23). He's got the Mean Green in position to reach the AAC title game heading into a huge showdown at UTSA on Saturday. Last week: 21

title: At MLB GM Meetings, the Phillies are at a crossroads while the Mets have a clear priority - CBS Sports
description: The NL East rivals both hope to be in contention in 2027 and have plenty of roster questions to answer
body:
The NL East rivals both hope to be in contention in 2027 and have plenty of roster questions to answer
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:44 am ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        LAS VEGAS — The Phillies are at a crossroads. A team that is still full of promise. A team that can compete with some of the best clubs in the league. A team that has World Series hopes. But also a team whose core consists of aging superstars. "We have a lot of high-end salary players, and they're not young, they're not old, but they're in that age bracket that you have to make a decision," Phillies president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowksi said Tuesday during GM Meetings. "Maybe we have enough high-end players, and we need to complement them with other players overall. That's a decision we have to make."With a likely lockout looming and the financial structure of baseball's future unclear, the Phillies have a projected payroll of $247 million for 2027. Roughly two-thirds, or approximately $164 million of that money, will go toward players who are 34 or older, including household names such as Bryce Harper, Kyle Schwarber, and Zack Wheeler. All three had quality seasons in 2026, but it's fair to question whether this team has reached its ceiling. Wheeler is entering his age-37 season, while Harper and Schwarber are entering their age-34 seasons. That figure above doesn't account for Trea Turner, an aging shortstop who will turn 34 in June, or Aaron Nola, who also turns 34 that month. Turner and Nola will make a combined $51.8 million in 2027.
"Right now we need an outfielder," said Dombrowski. "You're talking about an outfielder, you're talking about some right-handed hitting, a utility infielder, a bit more in the bullpen."Can Dombrowski do it all? Especially in a market and a game that is defined by uncertainty this offseason? "I don't know," he said. "It might be hard because they all cost money, too." Whether it's through free agency, trades, or both remains to be determined. If the Phillies do spend in free agency, Seiya Suzuki remains on the Phillies' shortlist of possible options. 
Despite the unpredictability surrounding the 2027 season and Philadelphia's financial commitments to aging players, Dombrowski acknowledged that owner John Middleton remains willing to spend if the right opportunity presents itself.Still, building from within provided a good amount of the tenor during Dombrowski's media availability. The Phillies' leader was adamant regarding infield prospect Aidan Miller, intimating that the 22-year-old is certainly a real possibility as a key contributor — even more so with the struggles of Turner at shortstop in 2026."I really am not going to ever anoint a young player a position," Dombrowski said. "I do think he has the capabilities, and it's just not me. Anybody that's seen him, and people from other organizations probably saying, 'Wow, you still have to earn the spot, but I think that, as it stands, that would be very helpful for us to have that consideration.' And frankly, I'm hoping he does. I'm not giving it to him. But I'm hoping that he does."  

        
            
                Ranking the top 50 MLB free agents for the 2026-27 offseason, plus landing spots for every player
                
                    Mike Axisa                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Mets focused on SkubalA fellow should-be NL East contender is connected to the best free agent on the market.Left-hander Tarik Skubal will reportedly meet with the Mets next week. The incumbent Dodgers, according to general manager Brandon Gomes, have also been in contact with Skubal. The expectation is that those two sides will meet at some point as well, Gomes said at the GM Meetings Tuesday. While other teams, including the Padres are expected to make a run at Skubal, the Mets and Dodgers are currently viewed as the frontrunners. The Mets are coming off an abysmal season, finishing at the bottom of the National League East with a 74-88 record. Surely the club is in need of starting pitching, posting a 4.47 rotation ERA, the seventh-worst mark in baseball. David Stearns, the Mets president of baseball operations, elected not to comment on the Skubal sweepstakes, a customary practice this time of year, but spoke around the team's needs. 
"Having a complete rotation is really important, and that includes having pitchers who can successfully get you through a postseason and get you through a playoff series," Stearns said. "We've seen over and over again in the playoffs that that can be constructed in a variety of different ways, and so we're open to doing it in any way possible." Skubal, certainly, would offer New York an anchor to its rotation. An ace that the Mets haven't seen since Jacob deGrom. But he isn't a sudden fix to all of the Mets' pitching woes. Unquestionably, talented depth also stands at the forefront of some of the team's needs. Consider what they have lost. The club traded Freddy Peralta to the Rays at the deadline after a bad first half with New York. He turned a corner once he got with the Rays and helped lead them to a World Series. Also at the deadline, the club traded Clay Holmes, a converted starter, to the Cubs. 
Both pitchers are now free agents. Meanwhile, Kodai Senga and Sean Manaea, two veterans who have underperformed in recent years, are set to become free agents after the 2027 season (Senga has a $15 million option for 2028 that will likely be declined).Skubal is a logical fit in Queens, especially if Steve Cohen is ready to open his wallet."Every situation is unique," Stearns said. "It's been well-publicized, even since I've been here, we've engaged in extremely long-term negotiations for pitchers. We will do so again, but the situation matters. The specific circumstances matter. We do have to look at every individual pitcher on a case-by-case basis."
